title: Neighboring Bitwise XOR
statement:
The array `derived` of length `n` holds only 0s and 1s. It is claimed to come from some array `original` of length `n`, also made only of 0s and 1s, by XOR-ing each element with its right-hand neighbour around a circle:

- `derived[i] = original[i] XOR original[i + 1]` for every `i < n - 1`;
- `derived[n - 1] = original[n - 1] XOR original[0]` (the last element wraps around to the first).

Return `true` if at least one such `original` produces exactly `derived`, and `false` if none does.
notes:
## Intuition

A direct approach guesses `original[0]` (0 or 1), rebuilds every later bit from `original[i + 1] = original[i] XOR derived[i]`, and checks whether the final wrap-around pair matches. There is a shortcut: every `original[j]` is used in exactly two entries of `derived` (paired once with its left neighbour and once with its right). XOR-ing all of `derived` therefore XORs each `original[j]` with itself, which is 0. So a valid `original` forces the XOR of `derived` to be 0. Conversely, if that XOR is 0, the rebuild from `original[0] = 0` satisfies the wrap-around pair automatically, so an `original` exists.

## Approach

1. Start `total` at 0.
2. XOR every `bit` of `derived` into `total`.
3. Return whether `total` is 0.

## Example 1, step by step

`derived = [1, 1, 0]`. `total` goes `0 -> 1 -> 0 -> 0`. It ends at 0, so the answer is `true`; indeed `original = [0, 1, 0]` works.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over `derived`.
- Space: O(1): a single running value.

## Pitfalls

- With `n = 1`, the only entry is `original[0] XOR original[0] = 0`, so `[1]` is impossible; the XOR rule already says so.
- Counting 1s works too (their count must be even), but mixing up "even" and "odd" flips every answer.
- Do not forget the wrap-around entry when rebuilding `original` by hand; it is the only constraint that can fail.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `derived` | the given XOR of each pair of neighbours |
| `total` | XOR of all values of `derived` seen so far |
| `bit` | the current value of `derived` |

narration.1: derived holds the XOR of each element of original with its neighbour around the circle.
narration.2: Start the running XOR at 0, the value that changes nothing.
narration.3: Visit every entry of derived once.
narration.4: Fold the entry into the running XOR.
narration.5: After the loop, total is the XOR of all of derived, where each original bit appears twice.
narration.6: Paired bits cancel, so a valid original exists exactly when the total is 0.
